title: Chapter 205: She Is My Sister
html:
“Close the door, quickly.” The woman retreated into the room as though conscious of how alarming she looked.

“All right.” Chen Ge left the door slightly ajar. Before venturing farther inside, he had already planned his escape. He stood in the center of the living room and surveyed it. The woman sat on the edge of the bed and drew a thin blanket around herself. “Ignore the mess. Sit wherever you like.”

The apartment was not particularly messy, but medicine bottles lay everywhere. Chen Ge picked one up at random; its label was filled with terms he barely understood.

“Don’t touch my things,” the woman snapped. Suspicion filled her eyes. “What’s in your backpack? You don’t look as though you came to buy property.”

“The bag may be old, but it holds my life savings.” Chen Ge improvised. “The apartment is in a good location, but can you lower the price?”

“It’s a large apartment. If I didn’t need money, I wouldn’t sell it.” Her unnaturally white skin unsettled Chen Ge.

“If you don’t mind my asking, what illness has forced you to sell your home?” Chen Ge had no intention of buying it; he wanted information.

“Cancer.” She pointed to her face. “Long-term chemotherapy made me lose my hair and eyebrows.”

“I’m sorry.” It was the expected response.

“Now I only want to live as long as I can. I ask for nothing more.” Selling her home to prolong her life sounded plausible, but the story did not withstand scrutiny.

“Let’s discuss the price.” The woman had already made a major concession: her asking price was thirty percent below market value. “If you agree, we can sign the papers tomorrow.”

“I don’t want to take advantage of you, but the price is still high.” Chen Ge assumed the role of a calculating buyer.

“A price like this is still high?”

“I sympathize with your condition, but I asked around before coming. The apartment was supposedly haunted several years ago, which is why it still hasn’t sold.” Chen Ge patted his backpack. “I’m braver than most, but I don’t have much money. That’s why your listing caught my attention.”

Realizing he knew the truth, the woman asked, “How much are you prepared to pay?”

“One-tenth of the market price. That’s all I have.”

“One-tenth?!” The woman scoffed. “And you said you’re not trying to take advantage of me?”

“The place is haunted. If I weren’t short on money, I would never consider it.” Chen Ge had fully inhabited his role. Feigned hesitation and sympathy entered his eyes. “Why don’t we meet halfway? I know you need the money for treatment, so I can borrow from family and friends, but your price is still too high.”

The long vacancy had perhaps begun to weigh on her. After a silence, she said, “One-tenth is impossible. My absolute minimum is half the market price. If you accept, I’ll have a lawyer prepare the documents tomorrow. Otherwise, leave.”

“Half…” Chen Ge lowered his head as though considering it.

“Don’t believe the rumors. No tenant has ever been hurt, so how could the place be haunted?” The woman reclined on the bed. Sensing his resolve weaken, she pressed her advantage.

“Don’t lie to me. A security guard personally saw a white figure enter your apartment several years ago, and the police confirmed his account. You weren’t home that night, so perhaps you never learned the details.” Chen Ge followed the thread, probing for the information he wanted.

“How could I not know what happened in my own home?” She sighed, conflict clouding her eyes. “I didn’t want to tell you for fear of scaring you, but that white figure wasn’t a ghost.”

“Not a ghost?” Chen Ge’s pulse quickened. The conversation was yielding more than he had expected.

“Yes. The white figure was my sister. She was a psychiatric patient who had recently been released.” Pain twisted the woman’s face, and she coughed violently for several minutes. “My sister did something terrible as a child, which was when her illness was discovered. She was committed afterward and released only four or five years ago.”

“Something terrible? How serious was it?” Her sister matched Patient No. 2’s history, and Chen Ge listened more closely.

“Serious enough to ruin her life.” The woman sighed. “Her condition is unusual. She required isolation because she could endanger the public. If the police found her, they might take her from me and confine her in another psychiatric hospital.”

“So you hid her in your home?”

“After ten years of treatment, she had improved greatly.” Conviction entered the woman’s voice. “How many decades does anyone have? She suffered enough in her youth. She deserved the chance to live normally.”

Something in her account felt wrong. “So you hid your sister in your apartment, but she slipped out and frightened the other tenants? That’s the truth behind the haunting?”

“Yes. The haunting existed only in their imagination.”

“What happened to your sister, then? With you this ill, shouldn’t she be caring for you?”

“I have no idea where she disappeared to. I haven’t seen her since that night.” Helplessness softened the woman’s face. “She is my only family. Sometimes I return to Fang Hwa Apartments, hoping she’ll appear.”

“I understand. If no one else makes an offer, could you hold the apartment for me? I’ll arrange a loan tomorrow.” Chen Ge sounded sincere, but he only wanted to keep her cooperative while he investigated something urgent.

“All right. I’ll see you tomorrow.” She ended the conversation and sagged against the headboard, exhausted.

“See you tomorrow.” He picked up his backpack and left.

The moment the door closed between them, both their expressions changed. Remaining in the corridor, Chen Ge searched the few English terms he remembered from the medicine label.

“Just as I thought—she’s deeply suspicious. Those medicines have nothing to do with cancer. Most promote wound healing or prevent infection.”

Chen Ge hailed a taxi back to Fang Hwa Apartments. On the way, he called Inspector Lee and reported everything he had discovered at Xin Kang Apartments.
